_README: Sample chapter shipped with the public repo so the project builds and is playable straight after cloning. It demonstrates all six question types. Real course content lives in separate ch*.json files that are not published. Delete this file once you have added your own chapters.
title: Sample Chapter — How This Game Works
subtitle: A demo of all six question types

questions.prompt: How many times must a question be answered correctly before it locks in as mastered?
questions.explain: Three correct answers on separate encounters. This is the whole point — recognising an answer once is not the same as knowing it. The threshold is MASTERY_BOX in src/app.js.

questions.prompt: What happens when you get a question wrong?
choices: Nothing — it stays at the same level
It drops two boxes, so it comes back around quickly
It is removed from the pool
questions.explain: A miss knocks the question down two Leitner boxes. Questions you struggle with are shown far more often than ones you have locked in.

questions.prompt: Select ALL question types this engine supports.
questions.explain: Six types: mc, multi, match, order, fill, and scenario. Drawing and audio are not supported.

questions.prompt: Match each question type to what it asks the student to do.
pairs: Choose one correct option from a shuffled list
Select every correct option — the set must be exact
Arrange items into the correct sequence
Type the answer, matched ignoring case and punctuation
questions.explain: Terms and definitions are both shuffled each time, so students cannot learn positions instead of content.

questions.prompt: Put the steps for adding new content in the correct order.
items: Edit or add a JSON file in content/
questions.explain: The build validates every question before it bundles. A typo fails the build rather than reaching students — see build.js.

questions.prompt: Which single command builds and validates all content? npm run ________
questions.explain: npm run build. Matching ignores case, punctuation and extra spaces, and you can list several accepted spellings in the answer array.

questions.prompt: A student has answered 70% of a chapter's questions correctly three times each, but cannot open the next chapter. Why?
choices: They need to complete a timed exam first
Chapters unlock at 80% mastery, so they are 10 points short
The next chapter has not been published yet
questions.explain: UNLOCK_AT is 0.8 — a chapter must be 80% mastered before the next one opens. Raise or lower it in src/app.js to change how strict the gating is.

questions.prompt: A student plays without entering a class code. What is true? Select all that apply.
choices: They still get the full game
Progress saves in their browser only
Their results appear on the instructor dashboard
They are blocked after one round
questions.explain: The class code is optional. Without one the game works fully but progress never leaves the device, so it does not reach the dashboard.
